title: Dedicated SLA probing and customer acceptance framework
creator: Aisha Shah
description:
Goal: build an end-to-end harness and test methodology that validates Dedicated capacity SLAs and produces a reproducible customer acceptance test (CAT) package. The CAT package will be consumable by SEs and customers and will include a runner, reference datasets, scoring scripts, and a pass/fail rubric that maps to contract guarantees.

Scope:
- A portable load probe (k8s job + local runner) that can exercise the serving runtime end-to-end with realistic traffic shapes (burst, steady, chat-like).
- Benchmarks and measurement methodology for sustained throughput, tail latency (p95/p99), and per-token cost under different batching/kv-cache settings.
- Autoscaling/eviction probes: scripted scenarios that cause scale-up/scale-down and graceful degradation fallback to variant models.
- Customer Acceptance Tests (CAT): a reproducible runbook and artifact set that SEs and customers can run to accept Dedicated capacity installs.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: integrating with third-party traffic generators beyond our runner (we will provide adapters later), and long-term historical result storage (separate infra ticket).
acceptance_criteria: A reusable harness (Docker image + k8s job template) that runs a predefined workload and emits a summarized JSON report.

A deterministic CAT run that, when executed against a Dedicated pool sized per our capacity calculator, reports pass if p95 latency < 120ms at 100 RPS sustained with <10% throughput variance over 10 minutes.
A documented methodology page describing traffic shapes, sample sizes, and statistical treatment used to compute p95/p99 and throughput guarantees.

Autoscales exercised and validated: scale-up within 90s of sustained 75% GPU utilization, scale-down cooldown observed and documented, and automatic fallback to smaller model variant demonstrated when capacity saturated.
Links to artifacts: dashboard URL, GitHub PR, and S3 results bundle included in the ticket before Done.
steps: Build probe image with configurable concurrency, sequence length, and prompt templates.
Create k8s job template that mounts secrets, points at target endpoint, and collects telemetry via Prometheus pushgateway.
Implement analysis script to parse raw traces and compute p50/p95/p99, sustained throughput, and error modes (429/5xx/timeouts).
Author CAT runbook for SEs including prechecks, size recommendation, and pass/fail guidance.
Run three smoke runs against staging Dedicated -- baseline, with KV cache disabled, and with high contention (simulated multi-tenant).
Record and publish results in S3 and link to console dashboard snapshots.
progress_updates: 2026-03-10 — Aisha Shah: Created ticket and aligned scope with PM/SE. Initial probe proto in python localkit exists (repo: github.com/redwood-inference/probe-client).
2026-03-11 — Marcus Li: Built first Docker image (probe:v0.1) and validated single-connection generation against staging endpoint. Observed p95 ~ 95ms at 20 RPS with kv-cache enabled.
2026-03-12 — Design review with Sofia Ramirez: agreed on CAT UI for SEs (simple pass/fail + downloadable artifacts). Added requirement to capture both latency histograms and token-level cost samples.

2026-03-13 — Marcus Li: Implemented k8s job template and Prometheus exporter. Ran 10-minute steady test at 60 RPS; sustained throughput stable but noticed tail latency spikes during burst window, creating follow-up ENG-24182 (tunable-batching-investigation).
2026-03-14 — Aisha Shah: Drafted methodology doc and uploaded initial S3 bundle s3://redwood-ci/cat/ENG-24178-run-20260314.tar.gz. Opened PR #4289 to add analysis scripts to repo.
blockers: OSS CUDA kernel incompatibility with our microbench harness on NGC 23.12 images — infra needs to vet a compatible node image (ticket ENG-24190).
Need access to a dedicated staging pool configured with autoscaler policies mirroring prod (waiting on infra ops approval, ETA 2026-03-16).
decisions: Use p95 latency at a configured payload distribution as primary SLA signal; p99 retained for incident diagnosis but not as pass/fail for CAT.
CAT will declare PASS only when run against a pool provisioned using our sizing calculator (to avoid undersized customer runs causing false failures).
Autoscale validation will use GPU-utilization-driven thresholds (scale-up at 75% avg util, scale-down after 180s below 40%) to mirror customer defaults.
